bib.title: Chapter 17. Scaling Disaggregated Prefill and Decode for Inference (AI Systems Performance Engineering)

question: How should a disaggregated prefill/decode LLM inference system be designed, routed, scaled and protected with QoS at very large scale?
contributions: Explains why separating prefill and decode removes interference and allows phase-specific hardware and parallelism
Describes prefill and decode worker design, KV cache transfer with NIXL, and decode memory management
Gives routing policies (threshold, latency-cost, remote-prefill score), Dynamo Planner autoscaling and QoS/early-rejection code

results.claim: DistServe reportedly served 7.4x more requests within strict latency SLOs than a state-of-the-art non-disaggregated baseline.
results.source: Zhong et al., DistServe (named, no citation printed)
results.setup: DistServe evaluation as described in the chapter intro; baseline unspecified beyond 'state-of-the-art'
results.quote:
DistServe’s evaluation showed the potential for serving 7.4× more requests within
strict latency service-level objectives (SLOs) compared to a state-of-the-art base-
line without prefill/decode disaggregation.

results.claim: In the colocated vs 2P1D example, the colocated single GPU sustains goodput of 1.6 RPS (min of ~3 RPS TTFT-bound and 1.6 RPS TPOT-bound).
results.setup: Colocated single GPU, SLO P90 TTFT 0.4 s and P90 TPOT 0.04 s, DistServe experiment (Fig 17-2)
results.quote:
As such, the goodput of the colocated configuration is only 1.6 RPS since both the TTFT and TPOT la-
tency SLOs need to be met.

results.claim: The 2P1D disaggregated configuration (2 prefill GPUs, 1 decode GPU) reaches 3.3 RPS per GPU goodput.
results.setup: 2 prefill workers at ~5.6 RPS each, 1 decode worker at ~10 RPS, same SLOs; 10 RPS / 3 GPUs
results.quote: As such, the goodput for the 2P1D configuration is 3.3 RPS per GPU.
results.note: Chapter then asks whether 3x cost is worth 2x improvement; the colocated 1.6 RPS is per 1 GPU, so the ratio is about 2x

limits: No experiments of its own: the numbers are DistServe figures, MLPerf SLOs and illustrative worked examples or config values.
Routing weights, thresholds and autoscale values are illustrative and the chapter says to set them empirically.
Chapter text contains an arithmetic slip (180 GB minus 70 GB printed as 122 GB) and says 'TPOT' where prefill throughput is meant (dedicated prefill nodes tuned for 'minimum TPOT').
Claims about OpenAI, Meta, xAI, Google adopting disaggregation are 'reportedly' and uncited.
vLLM flags (--max-seq-len-to-capture etc.) and Dynamo config shown may have dated; code shown is truncated in the text extraction.
practices: Keep prefill and decode in the same data center for realistic SLOs (Disaggregated Prefill and Decode Cluster Pools).
Use a decode-centric design where the decode worker receives requests and decides whether to prefill locally or offload (cluster pools section).
Use NIXL / GPUDirect RDMA for zero-copy KV transfer and pre-registered peer memory with large pinned windows; verify overlap in Nsight Systems (KV cache transfer).
Coalesce multiple PagedAttention blocks into ~128-token payloads before RDMA (Fig 17-4 caption).
Prefill: use high TP and FP8/FP4 on high-FLOPS GPUs; decode: little or no TP (often TP=1) with fused kernels and high-bandwidth GPUs (Phase-specific optimizations).
Prefill latency-first: little or no batching; throughput-first: batch 8-32 prompts; use adaptive batching windows of 2-10 ms (Optimizing for latency versus throughput).
Over-provision prefill capacity to absorb bursts and autoscale on metrics such as prefill queue length.
Do not offload short prompts or prompts with large prefix-cache hits; use effective length = prompt_length - prefix_cached_length (Routing factors).
Re-tune offload thresholds like PREFILL_LENGTH_THRESHOLD when hardware changes.
Set --max-num-seqs and --max-num-batched-tokens explicitly in vLLM and tune with --max-seq-len-to-capture to bound KV memory (Continuous batching).
Compute KV size from actual n_layers, n_kv_heads, head_dim and KV precision (Memory management).
Apply early rejection, prioritization and graceful degradation (disable remote prefill for low-priority requests) under saturation (QoS section).
Track TTFT and ITL/TPOT (p50/p95/p99) separately for prefill and decode nodes (Key Takeaways).
Prefer FP4 for weights and, where validated, activations; many stacks use FP4 weights with FP8 activations (Phase-specific optimizations).

terms.definition: the prefill work for one request delays the decode work of another
long or compute-heavy prefills at the front of the queue will block shorter, lighter requests behind them
the system receives a new request on the decode worker, which decides whether to prefill locally or offload
two prefill workers (two GPUs) and a single decode worker (one GPU)
admission control that refuses low-priority queries when the system is saturated
sending the same request to two different model sizes or two different routes and taking the fastest result
iteration-level batching that gathers all sequences ready for a next token at each step
